answer: Attention-depth registration requires each identity to accumulate verifiable dwell time in shared tasks before gaining voice, sampled across random checkpoints from a per-identity nadir of zero. Only identities crossing a threshold at the summit of the dwell distribution can propose work. Attackers pay sustained, parallelizable attention: hours of real participation per identity, not one-time tokens. A lagoon of idle sockpuppets accrues nothing, since decay resets scores during inactivity.
